open_points.subject: public_op:store.spool_file / A15 attempt-file discard rule
open_points.text: A15 rule 3: "only the files of that attempt are discarded, and files spooled earlier in the run stay." and public_op:store.spool_file Errors: "`refused` over a spool ceiling, nothing kept of that file or of any file that attempt spooled before (A15 rule 3)"
open_points.question: When one spool_file call crosses a spool ceiling after earlier files of the same attempt were already spooled, which operation is required to remove those earlier same-attempt files?
options: store.spool_file must atomically roll back all files of that attempt
the caller (runs/effects) must explicitly clean up prior same-attempt files
spooling for one attempt must be done in one bulk call so partial prior files cannot exist
open_points.default_guess: store.spool_file enforces rollback by attempt identity on refusal

open_points.subject: MCP read_spooled_file input contract
open_points.text: "`read_spooled_file` ... names it by its identity ... — the lookup identity; its digest, size and media type only describe it"
open_points.question: Are digest/size/media_type in read_spooled_file request required-and-validated against the record, optional metadata, or ignored entirely for correctness?
options: require them and refuse if any mismatches stored SpooledFile facts
accept them as optional descriptive fields and ignore for lookup/validation
require them syntactically but do not compare to stored facts
open_points.default_guess: use only identity fields for lookup and ignore descriptive fields

open_points.subject: public_op:store.read_records error surface
open_points.text: public_op:store.read_records Errors: "`unknown_reference` for the whole call when any named identity does not exist" versus Relations of store.read_records: "A call that passes other arguments is a defect of its caller and answers `internal_error` — so does one that omits an argument its relation names or passes one of another kind"
open_points.question: Is `internal_error` an official possible result of store.read_records for malformed relation arguments, and must callers handle it as part of the operation contract?
options: yes, store.read_records can return internal_error for malformed relation calls
no, malformed relation calls are prevented elsewhere and this op should expose only unknown_reference
malformed relation calls should be mapped to refused/invalid_request instead
open_points.default_guess: store.read_records may return internal_error for malformed relation arguments
